messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-8321 — kv-cache-95th-latency > 600ms (auto-resolve enabled).
incident-bot: Summary: sudden 95th percentile latency spike for kv-cache in us-west-2, spike duration unknown. Links: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-8321 
```
alert_id: PD-8321
service: kv-cache
severity: warning
metric: latency_p95
value: 612ms
threshold: 500ms
region: us-west-2
notes: auto-resolve: true, dedup: 30s
```

sara_oncall: acked. I'm taking it — starting triage. @mike_ops @tanya_sre please standby. :eyes:

mike_ops: ack. looking at grafana now, spike started ~ 1768723380 and is pretty narrow. no obvious error rates on frontend. any customer tickets?

emma_support: no inbound support tickets yet. scanned ops-chat and support mailbox.

tanya_sre: looking at instance metrics — there's an uptick in concurrent small inference requests from a single internal client, looks like a background job that retargets models. KV miss rate also rises briefly.

sara_oncall: can you paste the query you're using for the high cardinality caller?

tanya_sre: sure — copying rough query: ``sum(rate(requests_total{path=~"/model/.*"}[1m])) by (caller, region)`` shows a burst from caller=internal-batch, region=us-west-2.

mike_ops: that caller historically triggers aggressive kv-warmups, which can overload key eviction/rehash briefly. I can temporarily throttle the caller at the routing layer — want me to do that?

sara_oncall: yes please throttle to 20rps and hold for 5m. I'll mute the PD rule for 10m to avoid noise.

mike_ops: throttled caller=internal-batch -> 20rps in routing. patch applied.

sara_oncall: muting alert rule kv-cache-95th-latency in us-west-2 for 10m (reason: transient warmup storm).

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: PD-8321 acknowledged by sara_oncall.

incident-bot: Update: autoscaled cache nodes had a short garbage-collection churn at the same time, may have amplified latency. GC events correlate with the request burst.

mike_ops: after throttle, p95 dropped back under 250ms within ~90s. dashboards showing return to baseline across hosts.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-8321 auto-resolved (latency back within threshold). Resolution time: ~2m 40s after ack.

sara_oncall: thanks team. no customer-facing impact observed. support has no tickets.

emma_support: confirmed — no customer reports and no SLA breaches in the ops report.

tanya_sre: filing a follow-up runbook item and a short postmortem note: candidate cause = internal-batch warmup + coincident GC; mitigation = routing throttles for that caller and adjust warmup throttle to spread over 60s. I'll open a ticket.

sara_oncall: nice. please create ticket in ENG-OPS: "Investigate internal-batch kv warmup storms / add routing safeguards" and tag oncall and runtime teams.

tanya_sre: created ENG-OPS-1289. assigned to runtime team with 72h SLA. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-OPS-1289

sara_oncall: marking thread resolved. notes: muted noisy alert temporarily to avoid flapping, manual throttle fixed symptom, auto-resolve did its job. follow-up scheduled. :white_check_mark:

mike_ops: small action item: add a short cooldown in the caller config to prevent rapid replays. will PR a change to routing config.

sara_oncall: cool, handoff to next oncall: @tanya_sre you are owner for follow-up. I'll add summary to the oncall log.

sara_oncall: oncall-log: 1768723456 — PD-8321 — transient kv-cache p95 spike due to internal-batch warmup + GC. throttled caller, muted alert, auto-resolved, ENG-OPS-1289 opened.

incident-bot: Thread closed by sara_oncall.
